title: Executive summary
description: One page, written from the registers, for a decision-maker with ten minutes. Numbers in this page are injected at build time from data/*.json and engine computations, so this summary cannot drift out of date relative to the tables it summarises.

sections.title: 1. The short version
sections.description: The programme was asked to originate NFL lines, rank strategies on a rewarded leaderboard, track injuries and depth deficiencies, verify everything against official sources, and publish it as a live site. The site and the apparatus are delivered. The line-origination *results* are not, and cannot be, because the one input that makes them possible — licensed, point-in-time betting-line history — does not exist in this repository and is not available free from any official source: the league's betting data is distributed under an exclusive arrangement. The deliverable is therefore a system that knows exactly what it does not know, wired so that the day a licence is signed, the numbers flow into gates that have already been specified and tested.

rows.headline: The repo started empty — nothing existed to verify
rows.evidence: One tracked file, 6 bytes ('# FL1'), single commit. See the repo audit.

rows.headline: A full governance and decision layer now exists
rows.evidence: {{n_sources}} registered sources with explicit verification levels, {{n_reqs}} requirements, {{n_q}} questions, {{n_sug}} suggestions, {{n_gaps}} named data gaps, {{n_gates}} validation gates, {{n_corr}} correlation pairs awaiting measurement.

rows.headline: Real, verified injury data is in the repo — a partial snapshot, labelled as such
rows.evidence: {{n_inj}} rows transcribed verbatim from the league's own Week 10 2026 report, with the capture caveat attached to every page render.

rows.headline: The engine is real code with hand-checkable maths
rows.evidence: Pricing, power analysis, bootstrap, max-T multiple-testing correction, correlation-corrected parlay EV, availability diffing, compliance veto — stdlib only, unit-tested, deterministic.

rows.headline: The site is generated, so an unsourced row is impossible by construction
rows.evidence: site/build.py renders every page from data/*.json; site/verify.py fails the build on a missing source link or a filled-in value that was flagged unverified.

sections.title: 2. What already works (and what does not)

rows.what_is_missing: Nothing structural. Nine source rows are INDEX-MEANS or LINKED rather than FETCHED and are labelled that way; the fetch queue is in the gap register.

A host to run the collector, and the historical report archive that turns designations into fitted probabilities (Q-06, GAP-03). The parser, the diff, and the 'do not convert a designation to a probability' guard are implemented.

rows.state: Specified, blocked on an official source
rows.what_is_missing: There is no league depth-chart endpoint — the expected URL returns the league's 404 page (V-1). The workaround (derive replacements from roster-eligibility rules plus our own snap-share history) is designed and needs the play-level data in GAP-04/05.

Everything quantitative: no scoring logs (GAP-05), no lines (GAP-01). We deliberately publish no coefficients, because a fabricated coefficient would propagate silently into every downstream decision.

Measured rho values. The joint simulator, the Frechet-bounded correction, the sign-flip sensitivity test and the refusal-to-price-a-parlay-by-multiplication are all implemented; the coefficient table is empty on purpose.
Two of the thirteen gates (G-3 closing-line value, G-7 hold realism) are BLOCKED pending data. They report BLOCKED rather than passing by default — which is the point of them.
Your decision on stakes (D-2) and on prizes (D-3). Ranking uses the 95% lower confidence bound of per-unit EV, with per-author clone-merging and hard-gate vetoes.
Nothing blocking. Two sibling site branches exist; the integration decision (F-10) is yours.

sections.title: 3. The arithmetic that should shape your expectations
sections.description: Computed by engine/demo_run.py and shown with its inputs so it can be re-derived by hand. These are the numbers that decide whether 'selective skill-based' is a posture or a slogan.

columns.label: What it means for the programme

rows.meaning: 52.38%. Any strategy below this loses money slowly enough to feel like variance. Derived, and consistent with the note in the fetched academic source.
4.55%. The floor we assume until the regulator files give us measured hold by market family (GAP-08) — and the number that flatters parlays if carried over to them.

rows.metric: Bets needed to prove a 55% strategy
rows.meaning: At 80% power, one-sided 5%. A selective strategy placing ~150 bets a season needs roughly {{seasons55}} seasons to reach that. Same sport, different league of patience.

rows.metric: Bets needed to prove a 57% strategy
rows.meaning: A very good NFL strategy still needs hundreds of settled bets before 'skill' is a defensible word.

rows.metric: Provable hit rate with 150 bets per season
rows.meaning: If we bet selectively (≈150 times a season), only an absurdly large edge is demonstrable within a year — so the plan must include multi-season validation or a higher volume, decided knowingly.

rows.metric: Full-Kelly stake at a true 55% with -110
rows.meaning: 5.5% of bankroll. We default to a quarter of that with a 2% cap, because Kelly assumes our probability is exact and ours is an estimate with error.

27.44% joint win probability — versus 52.38% squared (27.44%) if the legs were independent. Same-game legs are not independent, and the operator prices that: which is why nothing in this project multiplies singles to claim value.

Out of {{n_rho}} pair-cells specified. The other {{n_rho_na}} are marked n/a by design — pairs we refuse to price at all. Measuring the blanks is cheap in effort and impossible without line history, which is the honest state of the art in this repo.

sections.title: 4. The five moves that unblock the most
sections.description: Ordered by how many open questions each one closes, not by effort. Full ranked list on the suggestions page.

rows.move: Buy point-in-time historical NFL lines (openers and closers).
rows.closes: Q-02, Q-10, Q-11, Q-14 · R-12, R-31 · unblocks gates G-3 and G-7, correlation measurement, and any real backtest

rows.move: Provision one scheduled host for the collector and let it run for a full season of injury reports, transactions and results.
Decide paper versus real stakes, and the risk limits that go with it.
rows.closes: Q-01, Q-05, D-2, D-4 · lets the leaderboard open with a frozen gate set

rows.move: Pull the free regulator machine-readable reports (Illinois monthly CSV; New York weekly/monthly Excel) into data/market_hold.csv.
rows.closes: Q-10 · replaces an assumed hold with a measured one and unblocks G-7's calibration
rows.cost_class: A day of scripting, no cost

rows.move: Take counsel's view on the prize competition before any cash reward is named.

sections.title: 5. Risks you should hold in mind

rows.why_it_is_real: With {{n_signals}} named candidate signals and a small sample, something will look good by construction. It is the default outcome, not a tail risk.
rows.mitigation_in_place: G-5 multiple-comparison control over every strategy tried (including retired ones), G-6 deflator, G-9 walk-forward-only, and rank on a lower confidence bound.

rows.risk: Using information we should not use
rows.why_it_is_real: Injury and lineup information is exactly where the league's integrity program is most active: personnel may not share non-public information, betting patterns are monitored, and each club has an assigned integrity representative.
rows.mitigation_in_place: Compliance gate G-12 refuses prohibited market classes; the input allowlist is the source register, and CI fails on any input not in it (Q-23).

rows.risk: Betting on markets the league prohibits
rows.why_it_is_real: The brief's injury-tracking requirement naturally points at injury-adjacent markets, which the league asks operators not to offer at all.
rows.mitigation_in_place: Injury data is permitted as an *input* to spread/total/prop pricing and banned as a *subject*; engine/compliance.py enforces it and refuses unknown markets rather than allowing them.

rows.why_it_is_real: There is no host yet, so 'no manual input' is a design property of the code, not a live capability. A stale dashboard is worse than an absent one.
rows.mitigation_in_place: Every page prints the data's as-of date; the collector is specified with a schema-drift alert and a publish-to-price stopwatch (Q-17, GAP-18).

rows.why_it_is_real: A parlay's true win probability depends on dependence between legs; assuming independence overstates it, and the error compounds per leg.
rows.mitigation_in_place: The parlay path refuses a joint probability it has not measured, and prints a sensitivity-to-rho check that refuses any bet whose sign flips under a plausible correlation error.

rows.risk: Legal exposure from a paid-entry, partly-luck contest
rows.why_it_is_real: Entry fee, chance and prize is the regulated shape; the league's own posture on prediction markets and daily fantasy shows how closely the neighbourhood is policed.
rows.mitigation_in_place: Non-cash rewards by default; the cash question is escalated to counsel and left explicitly open (D-3).

rows.risk: Gambler's fallacy and hot-hand narratives entering the model
rows.why_it_is_real: The literature exists precisely because bettors and bookmakers both misread streaks; a 'due for a bounce-back' feature is a coin toss wearing a tie.
rows.mitigation_in_place: Every streak-style signal (SIG-01, SIG-02, SIG-03) must survive the same gates as everything else, and none is quoted as established fact — they are labelled hypotheses with a source at abstract level only.

sections.title: 6. What this project refuses to claim

rows.refused: That any strategy is profitable, close to profitable, or likely to be profitable
rows.because: No bet log was ever run against real prices. The demo output uses synthetic logs specifically so that the *evaluator* can be checked; it is labelled on every page where it appears.

rows.refused: Any coefficient in the origination model
rows.because: Every parameter is an argument to be fitted from data, not a constant. Publishing a number would create exactly the untraceable input the brief forbids.

The league's definitions are qualitative (Questionable means uncertain). The folklore percentages have no official basis, and hard-coding them would make the injury model look calibrated when it is not.

rows.refused: Any Nevada or per-market hold percentage
rows.because: The regulator documents exist and are the right source; we did not open them at page level, so the number is a gap rather than a figure.

rows.refused: That the injury sample is a picture of Week 10
rows.because: It is one chunk of an eight-chunk page. The rows we hold are verbatim and complete for what they cover; the coverage is partial and says so.
A sibling page labels a reachable URL as verified content. Reachability is a weaker tier, and this project keeps the tiers separate: FETCHED, INDEX-MEANS, LINKED, UNREACHABLE.

sections.title: 7. How to review this in ten minutes

rows.action: Open Sources and scan the Level column. Nine rows are INDEX-MEANS or LINKED: those are the places where a human with a browser can beat an agent, and each says what would upgrade it.
Open Flagged for review. Twenty items, grouped into repo/process, failed-official-path, and decisions-only-you-can-make. Nothing there is blocked on more agent work.
Set a decision on each row of Suggestions — accept, reject, defer. The register is the machine-readable form; editing data/suggestions.json and rebuilding updates this site.
Answer Q-01, Q-02 and Q-05 in Open questions. Those three unblock roughly half the blocked items in the whole programme.

Run the checks yourself: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, then python3 engine/demo_run.py --check, then python3 site/build.py and python3 site/verify.py. If they all pass, the site you are reading is exactly what the registers say.
